title: The Perfect Middle and Passive
subtitle: λέλυμαι — endings stacked on the reduplicated stem.
objectives: Form and conjugate the perfect middle/passive indicative of any ω-verb.
Recognize that the perfect middle/passive has no κ marker.
Understand the perfect middle/passive as expressing the state resulting from middle or passive action.
Distinguish perfect middle/passive from perfect active by form.

sections.heading: The perfect middle and passive
sections.body:
The perfect middle/passive uses the same reduplication as the active, but the endings are the primary middle/passive endings stacked directly onto the reduplicated stem. There is no κ marker.

λέλυμαι means 'I have been loosed' (passive) or 'I have loosed for myself' (middle), depending on context. As in the present and imperfect, the perfect middle and passive forms are identical. Context distinguishes.

sections.heading: The perfect middle/passive indicative: λέλυμαι
sections.body:
singular
  1st   λέλυμαι     I have been loosed / I have loosed for myself
  2nd   λέλυσαι     you have been loosed / you have loosed for yourself
  3rd   λέλυται     he/she/it has been loosed / has loosed for himself/herself/itself

  plural
  1st   λελύμεθα    we have been loosed / we have loosed for ourselves
  2nd   λέλυσθε     you (plural) have been loosed / have loosed for yourselves
  3rd   λέλυνται    they have been loosed / they have loosed for themselves

The endings are -μαι, -σαι, -ται, -μεθα, -σθε, -νται. No κ. The σ of -σαι often causes sound changes with the preceding stem consonant.

sections.heading: From Xenophon
sections.body:
Xenophon, Anabasis I.1.2: γέγονε πόλεμος.
'War has arisen.' γέγονε is the perfect of γίγνομαι (I become). The perfect means 'it has come into being' = 'it has arisen'.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 4.10 introduces the pluperfect and future perfect. The pluperfect expresses a state that existed in the past. ἐλελύκη means 'I had loosed'. The future perfect expresses a state that will exist in the future. λελύσομαι means 'I will have loosed'. Both tenses are rare.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate the perfect middle/passive of any ω-verb from memory and can distinguish it from the perfect active by form.
